# LinkedIn Reader

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. A LinkedIn feed is a self-selected stream of professional self-presentation: confident posts about a company or a market are marketing as often as analysis, there is a real risk of loss in any decision taken from feed sentiment, and no output here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the LinkedIn reader of himself65/finance-skills. Use it to read LinkedIn for financial research through opencli, which reuses your existing Chrome login session through its Browser Bridge extension, with no API keys and no cookie extraction. It reads your home feed (author, headline, text, reactions, comments and URL per post) so you can see what professionals and analysts are posting about a company, a market or an earnings release and gauge the professional sentiment, and it searches jobs with filters for location, seniority, job type, remote, company and posting date, with an optional details mode that returns full descriptions. The skill is read-only by design and says so plainly: it does not post, like, comment, connect, message or apply. Results are presented leading with what matters for the research question, market commentary and earnings reactions highlighted, and jobs listed with title, company, location, salary when available, posting date and URL. From the himself65/finance-skills repository (MIT). Honest caveats: this runs through your own logged-in Chrome session, so it sees...
